title: Calibration and validation harness against labelled reference corpus
claim: No harness computes correlation, error or CI coverage against any criterion measure; the 95% CI is derived arithmetically from word count.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no validate/calibrate script; only capture_golden.py which snapshots own output

impact_on_screened_person: Candidates are scored with an unvalidated number; no one can show the score predicts anything.
fix: Add scripts/validate.py that ingests a labelled CSV (text, criterion score), reports Pearson/Spearman r, MAE, CI coverage, per-language; fail CI if below thresholds.

title: Per-metric explanation of why a score came out as it did
claim: The report gives a composite VFS but no contribution breakdown tying weighted components to the final number or to what would change it.
impact_on_screened_person: A rejected candidate cannot learn which factor drove the outcome, and reviewers cannot challenge it.
fix: Add a 'contributions' block (weight x score per metric, rank, sensitivity) to compute_verbal_fluency_score and render it in the report.

title: Human-review workflow gate before any decision use
claim: Nothing forces a human reviewer to sign off; the output is directly consumable as a decision.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no review state, reviewer identity or sign-off record

impact_on_screened_person: Automated scores can become de-facto decisions with no accountable human.
fix: Add review record (reviewer, decision, rationale, timestamp) and mark reports 'UNREVIEWED - not for decision use' until signed off.

title: Score appeal and contestation path
claim: There is no mechanism for a screened person to contest a score or request rescoring with human review.

evidence.excerpt: **Do not use for consequential decisions.** These estimates must not be used for hiring, clinical assessment, academic evaluation, or legal proceedings.
ABSENT: no appeal, dispute or re-score API

impact_on_screened_person: A person harmed by a wrong score has no recourse, a legal exposure under automated-decision rules.
fix: Write an appeal procedure (intake, SLA, independent reviewer, rescoring with alternate text) and a tool recording appeal status.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/process/appeal-procedure.md exists and defines intake, SLA, independent reviewer and outcome records

title: Consent capture and purpose record before scoring
claim: Text is scored with no recorded consent, purpose or notice to the author.

evidence.excerpt: def tool_preprocess_text(text: str, lang: str) -> str:
ABSENT: no consent_id parameter or consent store

impact_on_screened_person: People can be profiled without knowing; violates notice/consent expectations under GDPR/UU PDP.
fix: Require a consent_id/purpose argument on the entry pipeline and refuse to score without it; store consent timestamp and text version.

title: API authentication for the MCP server
claim: The server exposes all tools with no authentication or caller identity.
impact_on_screened_person: Anyone reaching the server can score people's text; no accountability trail for who ran what.
fix: Add token auth middleware for non-stdio transports and attach caller identity to every call.

title: Rate limiting and abuse throttling
claim: No limits on call rate or payload size.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no rate limit or max text length

impact_on_screened_person: Enables probing the scorer to gaming-optimise text and denial of service for other users.
fix: Add per-caller rate limit and max input size with explicit errors.

title: Audit log export of every scoring decision
claim: No immutable record of who scored what, with which version and inputs hash.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no audit log writer or export

impact_on_screened_person: Screened persons and regulators cannot reconstruct how a decision was reached.
fix: Append-only JSONL audit log (timestamp, caller, input hash, tool versions, norms version, outputs) with export tool.

title: Versioned norms and model version stamped in every result
claim: Norms are loaded from unversioned JSON and outputs carry no norms/algorithm version, so results cannot be reproduced after change.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no version or effective_date field

impact_on_screened_person: A score from last year cannot be reproduced or compared; appeals cannot rerun the original logic.
fix: Add version/effective_date to norms files and algorithm version constant; include in all outputs and the golden fixtures.

title: Fairness dashboard of score distributions by language and group
claim: No tooling reports score distributions or impact ratios by language or any protected-proxy group.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no group-level distribution or four-fifths report

impact_on_screened_person: Adverse impact against Indonesian speakers or ESL authors goes undetected.
fix: Add scripts/fairness_report.py computing mean/SD, pass-rate ratios per language and optional labelled group over a batch.

title: Batch scoring with per-document results and error isolation
claim: Only single-text scoring exists; reviewers must script loops and one bad input breaks the flow.
impact_on_screened_person: Manual loops invite inconsistent handling and copy-paste mistakes across candidates.
fix: Add tool_score_batch accepting a list of documents returning per-document result or structured error.

title: AI-generated text detection flag
claim: Nothing flags text likely written by an LLM, whose fluency inflates VFS.

evidence.excerpt: ABSENT: no AI-text or authorship-integrity signal

impact_on_screened_person: Candidates using LLMs get inflated scores over honest ones; or honest candidates are mis-judged.
fix: Add an advisory heuristic flag (low-perplexity/uniformity) with explicit false-positive warning; never auto-penalise.

title: Writing-improvement feedback for the screened person
claim: Output is evaluative only; no actionable guidance for the author.
impact_on_screened_person: Candidates get a verdict but no path to improve, which reduces perceived fairness.
fix: Add 'suggestions' section from weakest metrics with sentence-level examples (repetition, long sentences).

title: Language expansion beyond English and Indonesian
claim: Unsupported languages are silently coerced to English.
impact_on_screened_person: Text in other languages is scored against English norms with no refusal.
fix: Return UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE instead of defaulting to en; define a language-pack interface for adding new languages with norms.

title: Refuse-to-score gate for insufficient or unsuitable text
claim: Scoring proceeds with only a confidence label even at under 30 words.
impact_on_screened_person: Tiny samples still yield an IQ and CI that downstream users treat as real.
fix: Return status INSUFFICIENT_TEXT with no IQ output below a configurable minimum word count.

title: Multi-sample aggregation for the same person
claim: Each text is scored independently; no way to combine several samples to raise reliability.
impact_on_screened_person: Single-sample scores are noisy; one bad writing day determines the outcome.
fix: Add aggregate_samples(person_id, results) returning pooled VFS with narrower, honest CI and between-sample variance.

title: Retention and deletion controls for submitted text
claim: No deletion or retention policy for candidate text and results.

evidence.excerpt: **Privacy.** Text submitted to the MCP server is processed locally. No data is sent to external services beyond the embedding model (downloaded locally on first use).
ABSENT: no purge or retention setting

impact_on_screened_person: Candidates cannot exercise erasure; stored text accumulates indefinitely.
fix: Define retention schedule and a purge tool; document in a DPIA.
acceptance_test: doc: docs/process/retention-and-deletion.md exists and states retention period and purge procedure

title: Structured machine-readable output schema with versioning
claim: Report JSON has no published schema, so integrators parse ad hoc.
impact_on_screened_person: Integrators mis-parse fields (e.g. N/A strings), causing wrong decisions downstream.
fix: Publish JSON Schema for the report and validate output against it in tests.

title: Confidence interval that reflects real measurement error
claim: CI width depends only on text-length tier, not per-metric variance or validation error.
impact_on_screened_person: Narrow CIs overstate precision for the person being judged.
fix: Compute CI from empirical residuals from the validation harness and bootstrapped metric variance.

title: Reviewer-facing evidence view with sentence citations
claim: Evidence is capped at three items per metric.
impact_on_screened_person: Reviewers cannot see why the score was reached beyond a few cherry-picked sentences.
fix: Add a verbose evidence mode returning all contributing sentences with their metric effect.

title: Reproducible run manifest with dependency and model hashes
claim: Results depend on unpinned spaCy models and libraries with no manifest recorded.
impact_on_screened_person: The same text may score differently after an upgrade and nobody can tell why.
fix: Emit a manifest (library and spaCy model versions) with each result.

title: Accommodation mode for non-native writers and disabilities
claim: No option to adjust interpretation for ESL authors, dyslexia or assistive tools.
impact_on_screened_person: Protected groups get systematically lower scores without any adjustment path.
fix: Add accommodation flag that suppresses IQ/edu mapping and requires human review.

title: Dry-run / what-if comparison between norm versions
claim: Cannot see how a candidate's score would change under revised norms.
impact_on_screened_person: Norm changes silently alter outcomes with no impact analysis.
fix: Add compare_norms(text, version_a, version_b) tool.

title: Interpretation guide embedded in every report for non-technical reviewers
claim: Disclaimers are optional and appear only with a verbose flag.
impact_on_screened_person: HR reviewers may never see the limitations that apply to the score.
fix: Always include a short mandatory limitations block in the report and scores-only output.

title: Configurable decision-use policy flag (screening vs. practice mode)
claim: No distinction between self-assessment use and employer/admissions use.

evidence.excerpt: **Do not use for consequential decisions.** These estimates must not be used for hiring, clinical assessment, academic evaluation, or legal proceedings.

impact_on_screened_person: The README forbids hiring use while the product is marketed for it, so behaviour is not enforced.
fix: Add use_mode parameter; screening mode requires consent, review and validation evidence to be present.
